text:
Jordan: Quick follow-up after the RFC meeting. I'm worried about combinatorial explosion if we let customers tweak low-level quant knobs. Proposal: expose a small "precision contract" surface (contract_id + optional compact_override_token) instead of a full DSL. Thoughts?

Priya: I like contract_id approach. Keeps runtime decision cheap. compact_override_token needs limits (size, allowed keys) or we risk too many telemetry dims. :eyes:

Leo: The main useful axes we've seen in perf/QA are: stable_kv_cache=true/false, attn_chunk_size, rounding_mode, and per-layer-calibration-scale. We should only allow attn_chunk_size and cache policy in overrides; calibration-scale must be part of curated contracts.

Diego: Agree. Also enforce per-tenant override quota + expiration. We should mint short-lived compiled tokens signed by validator service that the runtime verifies via cache lookup. Runtime only checks token signature OR local cache entry. No per-request network hop in the common case.

Jordan: Sketch of compiled token format idea: base64(signature|contract_id|override_digest|ttl). Validator service returns compiled_token and a compiled_profile_id that maps to runtime-ready blob.

Priya: How do we prevent risky combos that break quality? Validator must run checks: run lightweight shadow eval (few prompts) + check degscore delta threshold, or consult historical model-specific heuristics. If fails, reject.

Leo: Shadow eval adds latency to compilation but that's fine (one-time). We also need a deterministic fallback: runtime should map unknown/invalid compiled tokens -> contract_id default. No retries.

deploy-bot: INFO: rollout scheduled canary/precision-contract-shim -> 3% for 12h. See: https://go/ops/canary/precision-contract-shim

Diego: Telemetry implications: record compiled_profile_id, contract_id, override_keys_used, and degscore_cohort. But aggregate keys to limit cardinality: (contract_id, coarse_override_bucket, safety_tier).

Priya: Also add a metric for "compile_failures" with reason tag (shadow_eval, schema_violation, quota_exceeded). That will help ops and product.

Jordan: Security question: allow overrides in Private deployments? I propose: Private = disabled by default; Dedicated = disabled unless approved via ticket; Hosted = enabled with whitelist & quota.

Leo: One more runtime detail: cache key naming. Use stable prefix: precision:compiled:{compiled_profile_id}:{model_hash}. This keeps keys bounded per model variant. TTL default 24h, but prewarm during deploy or on profile publish.

Priya: Example flow in docs snippet:
```
# client -> server
POST /generate { contract_id: "balanced_v2", compiled_token: "ey..." }
# runtime -> local cache
blob = cache.get("precision:compiled:cpid123:modelabc")
if not blob:
  blob = validator.fetch_compiled(cpid123)  # rare path, fallback to contract
apply(blob.profile)
```

Diego: Ops playbook draft: (A) detect degscore increase > 0.05 vs baseline -> auto rollback to contract default; (B) compile_failures spike -> block new compiled tokens; (C) per-tenant violation -> revoke tokens.

Jordan: Action items: (1) Priya to draft whitelist + compile validation steps; (2) Diego to prototype signed compiled_token format and cache semantics; (3) Leo to add runtime fast-path checks and fallback mapping; (4) Jordan to update RFC with decision and sample compiled_token.

Priya: I'll also build a simple dashboard template with the aggregate dims Diego suggested.

deploy-bot: NOTE: canary started for precision-contract-shim at 8743210600.

Jordan: Thanks team. Goal: finalize follow-up doc by end of week so SRE/legal can sign off on Private gating.
